messages.subject_clean: How to convert from blavaan object to a stanfit object?
messages.body_plain:
Excellent! Thank you very much for your help!

On Tuesday, January 31, 2023 at 7:13:53 PM UTC+1 Ed Merkle wrote:
> If fit is the blavaan object, I think you want:
>
> stanobj <- blavInspect(fit, "mcobj")
>
>
> Ed
>
>
> On Tue, 2023-01-31 at 07:19 -0800, AM wrote:
> > Hi,
> >
> > I am using the high performance cluster at my university and the maintainers require us to send each chain as a separate job to the cluster. So if I have four chains, then I will end up with four different fit files.
> >
> > When I work directly with Stan, I can merge the files using the sflist2stanfit function. However, that doesn't work with blavaan objects.
> >
> > How can I convert blavaan objects to stanfit objects so that I can use the sflist2stanfit function? Alternatively, how can I merge the resulting files from four different chains?
> >
> > Note: I ensured that the chains were different by using the bcontrol argument in blavaan and setting the chain ID there, e.g. bcontrol = list(chain_id = 2) for the second chain.

messages.subject: Re: Standardized factor scores
messages.body_plain:
bayessdb<-read.csv(file.choose(),sep=";",header= T)
Gir="Giriskenlik=~Gir1+Gir2+Gir3+Gir4+Gir5+Gir6+Gir7+Gir8"
Fit1 <- bcfa(Gir, data=bayessdb, save.lvs=TRUE,
             n.chains = 3, burnin = 500, sample = 1500)
summary(Fit1)
coef(Fit1)
fitMeasures(Fit1)
summary(blavFitIndices(Fit1, pD="dic"))
blavPredict(Fit1)
blavFitIndices(Fit1)

.
....
..........

Computing posterior predictives...
Error in getGlobalsAndPackages(expr, envir = envir, globals = globals) : The total size of the 8 globals exported for future expression (‘FUN()’) is 630.69 MiB.. This exceeds the maximum allowed size of 500.00 MiB (option 'future.globals.maxSize'). The three largest globals are ‘lavmcmc’ (329.29 MiB of class ‘list’), ‘lavobject’ (301.33 MiB of class ‘S4’) and ‘FUN’ (31.11 KiB of class ‘function’)

I am so sad. I don't know what to do

> Ibo

The error messages you are getting are about some minor issue about the calculation of pD, which is a metric of "effectve number of parameters" use by WIAC and LOO, each have a different calculation for their respective pD.
>
> If you use LOO for model comparison, you dont need to pay attention to tjose errors, as they are only related to WIAC. Even woth the low percentage of problems, I wouldnt worry about it.
>
> Further, these are not related to the calculation of factor scores. for that you need to use the blavPredict() function which doesnt use any if these metrics for it
>
> for the blavFitIndices() function, you dont need to worry about this error warning as it uses the LOO metric by default, and your errors are not related to it
>

messages.subject: Re: Standardized factor scores
messages.body_plain:
İbrahim,

I believe that the waic issue was resolved in previous emails (use loo instead of waic). In your email below, I think your problem is the "out of memory" error at the bottom. Assuming that your computer has extra memory, you could increase the maximum allowed amount of memory. See:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/40536067/how-to-adjust-future-global-maxsize

If your computer doesn't have extra memory, then I would recommend setting save.lvs=FALSE, run the model, then run the fitMeasures and blavFitIndices commands. Then re-run the model with save.lvs=TRUE to do blavPredict(). The save.lvs=TRUE option uses lots of extra memory for the factor scores.

Ed

The loo and waic metrics are asymptotically equivalent, with loo being preferred. See:

https://avehtari.github.io/modelselection/CV-FAQ.html#21_How_are_LOO_and_WAIC_related

About factor loadings: you might take a look at the lavaan tutorial below, because many of those commands also work in blavaan. For factor loadings and other model parameters, the coef() or summary() command would work.

https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/index.html

Ed

Hi all,

Has anyone found any new solutions regarding the problem of 'hanging' that comes with this error message below?

“Chain 3: Exception: multi_normal_rng: Matrix covariance matrix argument is not positive definite  (in 'model_stanmarg' at line 1017)”

I am running a simulation and only very few of the conditions are giving me this hanging/error message issue. I'd like to be able to tell blavaan to conditionally stop/skip analyses with this error code, and move on to the next datafile.
Thank you in advance if you have any insights!

Best,
Liz

messages.body_plain:
Liz,

I had some off-list discussion with Gunnar about this (Gunnar started the thread) but am not sure that the details made it back to the list.

It seems that the hanging was due to extreme initial values. In blavaan 0.4-3, the initial values for each chain are randomly drawn from the priors. If you have non-informative priors, then those initial values sometimes are very extreme, and that seemed to cause Stan to hang. I have since changed the default way of generating initial values, to try to avoid the issue. If you can install blavaan from github, that includes the change along with other speedups for many models:

https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan

Or, if you stick with blavaan 0.4-3, then add

inits = "simple"

to your model estimation command (bsem/bcfa/blavaan). And if you don't care about the ppp, you could also set

test = "none"

which may help avoid the issue.

Ed

This might especially happen if your variables have lots of scores far from 0 (say, in the 100s). I am planning to change the defaults so they are more similar to rstanarm or brms, which scale with your data.

Ed

Stata 17: 10.6 seconds

That seems strange: 1 sec with Mplus but nearly 10 minutes with blavaan?  Do these differences make any sense?

fit <- bsem("stflife ~ agea + age2", data = data)

Christopher

On Monday, 25 April 2022 at 19:46:06 UTC+2 Ed Merkle wrote:
Yes, it should work for missing data but I think will require a custom lpdf in Stan. The problem is that you get to a missing data pattern with 1 observation, and the sample covariance matrix for that pattern is not positive definite, and then Stan throws an error when you try to model it. I think you can get around it by avoiding the constant terms in the density function.

Ed

On Mon, 2022-04-25 at 06:44 -0700, Terrence Jorgensen wrote:
right now, it only works for models with continuous variables, complete data, and fixed.x=FALSE.

Would the same trick work if implemented per missing-data pattern?  Perhaps problematic for unplanned missingness incomplete, but from planned-missing designs, it can be possible to compute the summary stats for the subset of variables relevant per missing pattern.  Vika and Ke-Hai capitalized on that for one of their proposed model-based transformation methods (extending Bollen-Stine for incomplete data).

This generally means that your system requires extra tools outside of R to compile a Stan model. An advantage of installing from CRAN is that they handle this compilation step for you. So I think the question is whether you have the desire/bandwidth to install some extra stuff on your system:

If no, I hope to get the new version of blavaan on CRAN within a week.

If yes, then you would want to look at the RStan "getting started" materials, especially the part about configuring a C++ toolchain:

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started

It can seem overwhelming if you've never done it before, but the process gets easier the more you do it.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: summary not printing fully
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the report, and it is indeed a problem that I have not been able to reproduce/diagnose. In the past, I have tweaked S3 and S4 summary methods to try to ensure that the blavaan method is used instead of lavaan. But the blavaan object "inherits" from lavaan, so that the lavaan summary() would be used if the blavaan method cannot be found. Maybe this could happen if you load a blavaan object without doing library(blavaan), but I can't imagine that everyone is doing that.

I also wonder whether you are using Rstudio? It seems that Rstudio does some package loading things that are different from regular R.

Thanks,
Ed

messages.subject: ppmc issues - Mu.hat
messages.body_plain:
When I run the (single group) analysis shown in the ppmc() help file,

HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
## fit single-group model
fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939,
            n.chains = 2, burnin = 1000, sample = 500)
AFIs <- ppmc(fit, thin = 10, fit.measures = c("srmr","chisq","rmsea","cfi"))

I see the following:

Error in 1:nrow(Mu.hat[[g]]) : argument of length 0

I am using R4.2.0 and blavaan 0.4-6.

Am really just getting started using blavaan so who knows what shenanigans I have got myself into!

messages.subject: Re: summary not printing fully
messages.body_plain:
Don't if it can help. I have a case that can reproduce the problem on my Windows machine, using Rgui, VS Code, and RStudio.

First, in a fresh session, run the following *without* loading blavaan:

# Code begins here
set.seed(8740325)
sigma <- matrix(.8, 4, 4)
diag(sigma) <- 1
dat <- MASS::mvrnorm(100, mu = c(x1 = 0, x2 = 0, x3 = 0, x4 = 0),
                          Sigma = sigma)
dat <- as.data.frame(dat)
mod <- "f1 =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4"
fit <- blavaan::bcfa(model = mod,
                     data = dat,
                     n.chains = 2)
summary(fit)
# Code ends here

This error will occur after the call blavaan::bcfa()

Error in blavaan(model = mod, data = dat, n.chains = 2, model.type = "bcfa", : could not find function "blavaan"

This is the search path:

> search()
[1] ".GlobalEnv"        "package:stats"     "package:graphics"  "package:grDevices" "package:utils"
[6] "package:datasets"  "package:methods"   "Autoloads"         "package:base"

Then run the code again, in the *same session*, with blavaan loaded:

# Code begins here
library(blavaan)
set.seed(8740325)
sigma <- matrix(.8, 4, 4)
diag(sigma) <- 1
dat <- MASS::mvrnorm(100, mu = c(x1 = 0, x2 = 0, x3 = 0, x4 = 0),
                          Sigma = sigma)
dat <- as.data.frame(dat)
mod <- "f1 =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4"
fit <- blavaan::bcfa(model = mod,
                     data = dat,
                     n.chains = 2)
summary(fit)
# Code ends here

bcfa will run normally. However, summary(fit) will not give the full report:

# Results begin here
summary(fit)

ended normally after 1000 iterations

  Estimator                                      BAYES
  Optimization method                           NLMINB

  Number of model parameters                         8

  Number of observations                           100

Model Test User Model:

  Test statistic                              -407.452
  Degrees of freedom                                NA

  Test statistic                                 0.597

  Degrees of freedom                                NA

Parameter Estimates:

Latent Variables:
                   Estimate

  f1 =~
    x1                1.000
    x2                1.107
    x3                0.988
    x4                0.995

Variances:
                   Estimate
   .x1                0.243
   .x2                0.146
   .x3                0.230
   .x4                0.179
    f1                0.775
# Results end here

But interestingly, blavaan does indeed come before lavaan in the search path:

> search()
 [1] ".GlobalEnv"        "package:blavaan"   "package:Rcpp"      "package:lavaan"    "package:stats"
 [6] "package:graphics"  "package:grDevices" "package:utils"     "package:datasets"  "package:methods"
[11] "Autoloads"         "package:base"

If I run the full code with library(blavaan) in a fresh session, the blavaan summary can be displayed normally:

# Results begin here
> summary(fit)
blavaan (0.4-6) results of 1000 samples after 500 adapt/burnin iterations

  Number of observations                           100

  Statistic                                 MargLogLik         PPP
  Value                                       -407.452       0.597

Latent Variables:
                   Estimate  Post.SD pi.lower pi.upper     Rhat    Prior
  f1 =~
    x1                1.000
    x2                1.107    0.085    0.950    1.281    1.000    normal(0,10)
    x3                0.988    0.085    0.833    1.172    1.000    normal(0,10)
    x4                0.995    0.081    0.850    1.161    0.999    normal(0,10)

Variances:
                   Estimate  Post.SD pi.lower pi.upper     Rhat    Prior
   .x1                0.243    0.046    0.165    0.346    0.999 gamma(1,.5)[sd]
   .x2                0.146    0.036    0.085    0.227    0.999 gamma(1,.5)[sd]
   .x3                0.230    0.043    0.160    0.324    1.000 gamma(1,.5)[sd]
   .x4                0.179    0.035    0.120    0.256    1.000 gamma(1,.5)[sd]
    f1                0.775    0.147    0.516    1.104    1.000 gamma(1,.5)[sd]
# Results end here

Interestingly, the search path is identical to that in the previous case:

> search()
 [1] ".GlobalEnv"        "package:blavaan"   "package:Rcpp"      "package:lavaan"    "package:stats"
 [6] "package:graphics"  "package:grDevices" "package:utils"     "package:datasets"  "package:methods"
[11] "Autoloads"         "package:base"

By the way, I intentionally used blavaan::bcfa() instead of just bcfa() because I wondered what might happen if I called bcfa() directly. In any case, this way to call a function is not that unusual (e.g., inside a package).

-- Shu Fai

messages.body_plain:
A quick followup, may or may not be related.

The error in the first run of my example, using blavaan::cfa() with out library(blavaan), is probably due to the following line:

https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan/blob/028556627c571d65fc8f237ef8bffa6c88cdf024/R/blavaan.R#L1061

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

Error occurred because blavaan is not in the search path, even though blavaan::cfa() is executed without problem.

This is the corresponding line in lavaan:

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/blob/17b67023c8816e041012da63ad57240f99c71ef3/R/xxx_lavaan.R#L2153

mc[[1L]] <- quote(lavaan::lavaan)

"lavaan::" is added. This makes sense because "lavaan::cfa()" and " "lavaan::sem()" are valid ways to call these functions (afaik, are also preferred ways to call them inside a package).

Not sure if changing

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

to

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan::blavaan)

will remove the problem of summary() in my example. I failed to compile the Rcpp code in my computer and so I could not test this in a fork.

If this can solve the problem in my example, maybe it can shed light on why that problem occurred in other scenarios.

-- Shu Fai

https://github.com/ecmer

messages.body_plain:
Shu Fai,

Thank you for your work! I can reproduce this example and am working with it now. I will email an update once I have a chance to test some changes.

Ed

On Wed, 2023-02-15 at 05:24 -0800, Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝) wrote:

> A quick followup, may or may not be related.
>
> The error in the first run of my example, using blavaan::cfa() with out library(blavaan), is probably due to the following line:
>
> https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan/blob/028556627c571d65fc8f237ef8bffa6c88cdf024/R/blavaan.R#L1061
>
> mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)
>
> Error occurred because blavaan is not in the search path, even though blavaan::cfa() is executed without problem.
>
> This is the corresponding line in lavaan:
>
> https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/blob/17b67023c8816e041012da63ad57240f99c71ef3/R/xxx_lavaan.R#L2153
>
> mc[[1L]] <- quote(lavaan::lavaan)
>
> "lavaan::" is added. This makes sense because "lavaan::cfa()" and " "lavaan::sem()" are valid ways to call these functions (afaik, are also preferred ways to call them inside a package).
>
> Not sure if changing
>
> mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)
>
> to
>
> mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan::blavaan)
>
> will remove the problem of summary() in my example. I failed to compile the Rcpp code in my computer and so I could not test this in a fork.
>
> If this can solve the problem in my example, maybe it can shed light on why that problem occurred in other scenarios.
>
> -- Shu Fai
>
> On Wednesday, February 15, 2023 at 11:52:24 AM UTC+8 Shu Fai Cheung wrote:
> > Don't if it can help. I have a case that can reproduce the problem on my Windows machine, using Rgui, VS Code, and RStudio.
> >
> > First, in a fresh session, run the following *without* loading blavaan:

> > # Code begins here

> > sigma <- matrix(.8, 4, 4)

> > fit <- blavaan::bcfa(model = mod,

> > # Code ends here

> > -- Shu Fai

> > On Wednesday, February 15, 2023 at 12:25:51 AM UTC+8 Ed Merkle wrote:
> > > Thanks for the report, and it is indeed a problem that I have not been able to reproduce/diagnose. In the past, I have tweaked S3 and S4 summary methods to try to ensure that the blavaan method is used instead of lavaan. messages.body_plain:
One update: the problem seems to happen if the blavaan namespace is loaded prior to library(blavaan). For example, the code below seems sufficient to get the wrong summary: (run it from a fresh session)

loadNamespace('blavaan')
library(blavaan)

HS.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, burnin=100, sample=100)

## lavaan summary:
summary(fit)

I might have to ask some R experts about this one...

Ed

On Wed, 2023-02-15 at 05:24 -0800, Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝) wrote:

> A quick followup, may or may not be related.
>
> The error in the first run of my example, using blavaan::cfa() with out library(blavaan), is probably due to the following line:
>
> https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan/blob/028556627c571d65fc8f237ef8bffa6c88cdf024/R/blavaan.R#L1061
>
> mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)
>
> Error occurred because blavaan is not in the search path, even though blavaan::cfa() is executed without problem.
>
> This is the corresponding line in lavaan:
>
> https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/blob/17b67023c8816e041012da63ad57240f99c71ef3/R/xxx_lavaan.R#L2153
>
> mc[[1L]] <- quote(lavaan::lavaan)
>
> "lavaan::" is added. This makes sense because "lavaan::cfa()" and " "lavaan::sem()" are valid ways to call these functions (afaik, are also preferred ways to call them inside a package).
>
> Not sure if changing
>
> mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)
>
> to
>
> mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan::blavaan)
>
> will remove the problem of summary() in my example. I failed to compile the Rcpp code in my computer and so I could not test this in a fork.
>
> If this can solve the problem in my example, maybe it can shed light on why that problem occurred in other scenarios.
>
> -- Shu Fai
>

messages.subject: Re: summary not printing fully
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for this example. I created a few more examples based on this one that hopefully may give some hints on the problem. All examples produced by reprex(). To run them in an interactive R session, they should be run in a fresh session.

This is the normal case, library(blavaan) only:

showMethods("summary")
#>
#> Function "summary":
#>  <not an S4 generic function>
library(blavaan)
#> Loading required package: lavaan
#> This is lavaan 0.6-14
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
#> Loading required package: Rcpp
#> This is blavaan 0.4-6
#> On multicore systems, we suggest use of future::plan("multicore") or
#>   future::plan("multisession") for faster post-MCMC computations.
showMethods("summary")
#> Function: summary (package base)
#> object="ANY"
#> object="blavaan"
#> object="blavFitIndices"
#> object="blavPPMC"
#> object="diagonalMatrix"
#> object="lavaan"
#> object="lavaanList"
#> object="mle"
#> object="sparseMatrix"
#> object="stanfit"

The summary method for blavaan is available, as expected.

The following example uses loadNamespace("blavaan") first and then library(blavaan):

showMethods("summary")
#>
#> Function "summary":
#>  <not an S4 generic function>
loadNamespace("blavaan")
#> <environment: namespace:blavaan>
showMethods("summary")
#>
#> Function "summary":
#>  <not an S4 generic function>
library(blavaan)
#> Loading required package: lavaan
#> This is lavaan 0.6-14
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
#> Loading required package: Rcpp
#> This is blavaan 0.4-6
#> On multicore systems, we suggest use of future::plan("multicore") or
#>   future::plan("multisession") for faster post-MCMC computations.
showMethods("summary")
#> Function: summary (package base)
#> object="ANY"
#> object="diagonalMatrix"
#> object="lavaan"
#> object="lavaanList"
#> object="mle"
#> object="sparseMatrix"
#> object="stanfit"

First, just loading the namespace does not make the method for blavaan available.
Second, if the namespace of blavaan is loaded first, even when blavaan is loaded by library(), the summary method for blavaan is not loaded.

Interestingly, this is not the case for lavaan, as shown in the following example:

showMethods("summary")
#>
#> Function "summary":
#>  <not an S4 generic function>
loadNamespace("lavaan")
#> <environment: namespace:lavaan>
showMethods("summary")
#>
#> Function "summary":
#>  <not an S4 generic function>
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-14
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
showMethods("summary")
#> Function: summary (package base)
#> object="ANY"
#> object="lavaan"
#> object="lavaanList"

messages.subject: Re: summary not printing fully
messages.body_plain:
Thanks, I have not had the chance to test any of these examples. But, if I recall the issue also tends to go away if knitting from an R markdown file.

On Wed, Feb 15, 2023 at 4:26 PM Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝) <shufai...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Thanks for this example. I created a few more examples based on this one that hopefully may give some hints on the problem. All examples produced by reprex(). To run them in an interactive R session, they should be run in a fresh session.
>
> This is the normal case, library(blavaan) only:
>
> showMethods("summary")
> #>
> #> Function "summary":
> #>  <not an S4 generic function>
> library(blavaan)
> #> Loading required package: lavaan
> #> This is lavaan 0.6-14
> #> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
> #> Loading required package: Rcpp
> #> This is blavaan 0.4-6
> #> On multicore systems, we suggest use of future::plan("multicore") or
> #>   future::plan("multisession") for faster post-MCMC computations.
> showMethods("summary")
> #> Function: summary (package base)
> #> object="ANY"
> #> object="blavaan"
> #> object="blavFitIndices"
> #> object="blavPPMC"
> #> object="diagonalMatrix"
> #> object="lavaan"
> #> object="lavaanList"
> #> object="mle"
> #> object="sparseMatrix"
> #> object="stanfit"
>
> The summary method for blavaan is available, as expected.
>
> The following example uses loadNamespace("blavaan") first and then library(blavaan):
>
> showMethods("summary")
> #>
> #> Function "summary":
> #>  <not an S4 generic function>
> loadNamespace("blavaan")
> #> <environment: namespace:blavaan>
> showMethods("summary")
> #>
> #> Function "summary":
> #>  <not an S4 generic function>
> library(blavaan)
> #> Loading required package: lavaan
> #> This is lavaan 0.6-14
> #> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
> #> Loading required package: Rcpp
> #> This is blavaan 0.4-6
> #> On multicore systems, we suggest use of future::plan("multicore") or
> #>   future::plan("multisession") for faster post-MCMC computations.
> showMethods("summary")
> #> Function: summary (package base)
> #> object="ANY"
> #> object="diagonalMatrix"
> #> object="lavaan"
> #> object="lavaanList"
> #> object="mle"
> #> object="sparseMatrix"
> #> object="stanfit"
>
> First, just loading the namespace does not make the method for blavaan available.
> Second, if the namespace of blavaan is loaded first, even when blavaan is loaded by library(), the summary method for blavaan is not loaded.
>
> Interestingly, this is not the case for lavaan, as shown in the following example:
>
> showMethods("summary")
> #>
> #> Function "summary":
> #>  <not an S4 generic function>
> loadNamespace("lavaan")
> #> <environment: namespace:lavaan>
> showMethods("summary")
> #>
> #> Function "summary":
> #>  <not an S4 generic function>
> library(lavaan)
> #> This is lavaan 0.6-14
> #> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
> showMethods("summary")
> #> Function: summary (package base)
> #> object="ANY"
> #> object="lavaan"
> #> object="lavaanList"
> #> object="mle"
>
> Similarly, loading the namespace of lavaan does not make its summary method available.
> However, the summary method of lavaan is available after library(lavaan) even if it is run after loadNamespace.
>
> So, it seems that the problem occurs for blavaan but not for lavaan. Maybe something in addition to loading the namespace first.
>
> Not shown above but I notice a similar problem with predict(), which is available in both lavaan and blavaan.
>
> Maybe something about method dispatch? I would love to learn more about this case.
>
> -- Shu Fai
>
> On Wednesday, February 15, 2023 at 11:13:32 PM UTC+8 Ed Merkle wrote:
> > One update: the problem seems to happen if the blavaan namespace is loaded prior to library(blavaan). For example, the code below seems sufficient to get the wrong summary: (run it from a fresh session)
> >
> > loadNamespace('blavaan')
> > library(blavaan)
> >
> > HS.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
> > textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
> > speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
> > fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, burnin=100, sample=100)
> >
> > ## lavaan summary:
> > summary(fit)
> >
> >
> > I might have to ask some R experts about this one...
> >
> > Ed

> > >
> > > Error occurred because blavaan is not in the search path, even though blavaan::cfa() is executed without problem.

> > >
> > > "lavaan::" is added. This makes sense because "lavaan::cfa()" and " "lavaan::sem()" are valid ways to call these functions (afaik, are also preferred ways to call them inside a package).

> > > Not sure if changing

> > > mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)
> > >
> > > to

Thanks, I have not had the chance to test any of these examples. But, if I recall the issue also tends to go away if knitting from an R markdown file.

On Wed, Feb 15, 2023 at 4:26 PM Shu Fai Cheung (

messages.subject: Re: summary not printing fully
messages.body_plain:
Thanks, it seems that the problem disappears if I list lavaan in the "Imports" field instead of the "Depends" field of DESCRIPTION.

By listing it in Imports, I think that people would not be able to automatically run other lavaan commands on a blavaan object. This might be a good thing, but I need to do more testing to figure out if this change would break anything.

Ed

On Wed, 2023-02-15 at 13:26 -0800, Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝) wrote:

> Thanks for this example. I created a few more examples based on this one that hopefully may give some hints on the problem. All examples produced by reprex(). To run them in an interactive R session, they should be run in a fresh session.
>
> This is the normal case, library(blavaan) only:
>
> showMethods("summary")
> #>
> #> Function "summary":
> #>  <not an S4 generic function>
> library(blavaan)
> #> Loading required package: lavaan
> #> This is lavaan 0.6-14
> #> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
> #> Loading required package: Rcpp
> #> This is blavaan 0.4-6
> #> On multicore systems, we suggest use of future::plan("multicore") or
> #>   future::plan("multisession") for faster post-MCMC computations.
> showMethods("summary")
> #> Function: summary (package base)
> #> object="ANY"
> #> object="blavaan"
> #> object="blavFitIndices"
> #> object="blavPPMC"
> #> object="diagonalMatrix"
> #> object="lavaan"
> #> object="lavaanList"
> #> object="mle"
> #> object="sparseMatrix"
> #> object="stanfit"
>
> The summary method for blavaan is available, as expected.
>
> The following example uses loadNamespace("blavaan") first and then library(blavaan):
>
> showMethods("summary")
> #>
> #> Function "summary":
> #>  <not an S4 generic function>
> loadNamespace("blavaan")
> #> <environment: namespace:blavaan>
> showMethods("summary")
> #>
> #> Function "summary":
> #>  <not an S4 generic function>
> library(blavaan)
> #> Loading required package: lavaan
> #> This is lavaan 0.6-14
> #> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
> #> Loading required package: Rcpp
> #> This is blavaan 0.4-6
> #> On multicore systems, we suggest use of future::plan("multicore") or
> #>   future::plan("multisession") for faster post-MCMC computations.
> showMethods("summary")
> #> Function: summary (package base)
> #> object="ANY"
> #> object="diagonalMatrix"
> #> object="lavaan"
> #> object="lavaanList"
> #> object="mle"
> #> object="sparseMatrix"
> #> object="stanfit"
>
> First, just loading the namespace does not make the method for blavaan available.
> Second, if the namespace of blavaan is loaded first, even when blavaan is loaded by library(), the summary method for blavaan is not loaded.
>
> Interestingly, this is not the case for lavaan, as shown in the following example:
>
> showMethods("summary")
> #>
> #> Function "summary":
> #>  <not an S4 generic function>
> loadNamespace("lavaan")
> #> <environment: namespace:lavaan>
> showMethods("summary")
> #>
> #> Function "summary":
> #>  <not an S4 generic function>
> library(lavaan)
> #> This is lavaan 0.6-14
> #> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
> showMethods("summary")
> #> Function: summary (package base)
> #> object="ANY"
> #> object="lavaan"
> #> object="lavaanList"
> #> object="mle"
>
> Similarly, loading the namespace of lavaan does not make its summary method available.
> However, the summary method of lavaan is available after library(lavaan) even if it is run after loadNamespace.
>
> So, it seems that the problem occurs for blavaan but not for lavaan. Maybe something in addition to loading the namespace first.
>
> Not shown above but I notice a similar problem with predict(), which is available in both lavaan and blavaan.
>
> Maybe something about method dispatch? I would love to learn more about this case.
>
> -- Shu Fai
>
> On Wednesday, February 15, 2023 at 11:13:32 PM UTC+8 Ed Merkle wrote:
> > One update: the problem seems to happen if the blavaan namespace is loaded prior to library(blavaan). For example, the code below seems sufficient to get the wrong summary: (run it from a fresh session)
> >

messages.subject: blavFitIndices Error: effective number of parameters exceeds the number of sample statistics
messages.subject_clean: blavFitIndices Error: effective number of parameters exceeds the number of sample statistics
messages.body_plain:
Hello fellow blavaan users,
I estimated SEMs with the same structure for different indicators (RTs, Accuracies, Drift Rates from Diffusion model) and for some models I get an error when calculating the Bayesian Fit Measures telling me that the number of parameters exceed the number of sample statistics. For others the Fit Indices are calculated just fine and are in a reasonable range.

I have checked with maximum likelihood estimation and all SEM for all indicators are identified. Anything else would be surprising given that they use the same number of indicators with the same model structure.
I suspect that this might be a problem with the devM calculation, because for the models that throw the error I get the warning:  sqrt(nonc/(dif.ppD * N)) : NaNs produced. This seems to mean that either the non-centrality value is smaller than zero, or the dif.ppD gets negative.

Has someone encountered this error before and can help with resolving this?
Thanks for your help.
Cheers, Gidon

messages.subject: Re: ppmc issues - Mu.hat
messages.body_plain:
Charles,

Thanks for this report and welcome to blavaan. This is a bug that will be fixed.

To work around the issue, you can add meanstructure=TRUE to your bcfa() command:

fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, n.chains = 2, burnin = 1000, sample = 500, meanstructure = TRUE)

It doesn't change the model in any way, it just ensures that there is a mean vector for the ppmc() command.

Ed

messages.body_plain:
Gidon,

I believe that is a warning instead of an error. So it is informing you that effective number of parameters is larger than a traditional parameter count, which may cause problems for some model summaries, but the software doesn't know for sure. It would be helpful to see the code for your model, as well as the fitMeasures() output for your model.

Ed

Thanks, it is better than before but could also use more improvement. Eventually, I will try to circle back and add some faster code that is dedicated to regression.

In the meantime, there is a chance that parallelization helps a bit more. In your bsem command, you could add

bcontrol = list(cores = 3)

Also, to parallelize post-estimation computations, you could try

library("future")
plan("multicore") ## mac or linux
plan("multisession") ## windows

Although I have heard that Rstudio might complain about the future package...

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Blavaan incredible slow...speed-up solutions?
messages.body_plain:
Thanks, the main bottleneck is figuring out how to code the Stan model for maximal speed/efficiency. In the traditional case, you cycle through each row of the data and evaluate the model likelihood for each row. But if you have complete data, you can use the sample covariance matrix and sample mean in place of each row of the data (at least, you can do it for SEM). If you have complete data and don't care about the means, you can use the sample covariance matrix and Wishart distribution. This gives better speed for large datasets because you no longer have to do computations for each row of the data.

And I might have already said it in a previous email, but if you don't care about the ppp (the model fit metric), then setting

test = "none"

should speed up some more.

Ed

messages.subject: Incorrect variance estimates
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've been working with blavaan to teach myself how to fit SEM with Bayesian inference in JAGS. To do this I fit the model below in blavaan and then tried to fit the same model with the "sem.jag" output. When I do this I'm getting very different estimates for the error variances between blavaan and a direct fit in JAGS. The error variance estimates from blavaan also differ dramatically from ML estimates in lavaan.

Here's the model. All five observed indicators are continuous:

model <- '
abundance =~ abu
habitat =~ mean_CC + mean_Food
urbanization =~ mean_UI + dist.city

habitat ~ urbanization
abundance ~ habitat + urbanization
'
Here are the issues I've noticed:

1) The latent variable "abundance" has a single indicator, so blavaan reports 0 for its variance estimate as expected. However, when fitting the model directly in JAGS, the term "theta[1,1,1]" corresponding to the variance for abu has an estimate of 13.59. Why wouldn't theta[1,1,1] be set to 0?

2) The error variances for the other observed indicators (mean_CC, mean_Food, mean_UI, dist.city) were all dramatically different than the corresponding theta estimates with a direct fit in JAGS, with significant convergence issues in JAGS (less so in blavaan, despite similar MCMC settings). Qualitatively the variance estimates directly from JAGS look more similar to ML estimates from lavaan than the blavaan estimates. It almost looks like the theta estimates in blavaan and the parameter names are all off by one row.

3) blavaan reports an error variance for each of the three latent variables, but the there are only two corresponding "psi" estimates with a direct fit from JAGS. It looks like blavaan is mistakenly reporting theta[5,5,1] for the "abundance" latent variance, which should be psi[1,1,1]. In the JAGS code, psi[1,1,1] is set to 1000 for some reason. I didn't expect this as there should be some estimated residual variance given abundance is an endogenous latent variable in the model.

Linked below is the "lavExport" folder which includes the sem.jag and semjags.rda files. I also added the R script and Rdata output for the model I used to fit directly in JAGS (using the sem.jag text output), along with a PDF highlighting discrepancies in output among blavaan, lavaan, and direct JAGS. I would greatly appreciate any thoughts on what might be causing the issues highlighted above.

https://www.dropbox.com/s/j5uy6r6dpmikyaf/lavExport.zip?dl=0

Many thanks,
Brad Cosentino

Hi, thanks for your suggestion. I will try using pD = “dic” then.

I fixed the loadings, because all latent factors only have two indicators and then freely estimating the loadings results in locally unidentified measurement models. I know that I would not need to do that as I could “borrow” information from the other measurement models, but from a psychometric perspective it mixes the measurement of a latent variable with its covariation to other latent variables. In this case, it would not be a serious problem, as the different latent variables are closely related being similar experimental tasks, but I still think it is good practice to aim for locally identified measurement models.

Gidon

The issue is that ths discrepancy in number of parameters and small models lead to negative or equal to 0 values in th formula for RMSEA.

On the issue of "local identification", it is recommended to have locally identified factors but is not a requirement. There is a debate if it is actually neccesary or not. I prefer it but there is not strong research in favor of one. Also, you can locally identify them without fixing them to 1, can equate the factor loadings, this way you would have only one estimated factor loading, and would be with std.lv <http://std.lv>=T , with a fix variance method of identification (which I prefer and recommend)

gPerf =~ l1*CD + l1*DE

messages.body_plain:
Hi Brad,

Thanks for the report, and I have had a chance to look at the model that you sent. There are a few different things going on that I will address in sequence.

Comparison to lavaan results: I have been devoting recent attention to the Stan side of blavaan (target = "stan") so first looked at how the model worked there. It turns out that blavaan's default prior distributions don't work well for your dataset, and your sample size is relatively low so that (i) the priors can make a difference, and (ii) Stan is good at finding extreme parameter values that are almost as good as the ones that lavaan reports. Maybe the simplest thing to do is scale your data, then use priors that are more informative. For example, below could work (though sometimes the chains still go off to more extreme values):

```
dat2 <- dat/10 ## assumes your original data is called "dat"

m2 <- bsem(model, data=dat2, dp = dpriors(lambda = "normal(0,.25)", beta = "normal(0,.25)"))
```

I don't see any obvious errors in how this Stan model is set up. I think the difficulty in convergence may reflect that the model is weakly identified, i.e., identified from a theoretical point of view, but there are also local optima of the posterior distribution that Stan is good at finding. And in the future, I hope to add an option in blavaan that automatically scales your priors to the scale of your data.

Your questions 1 and 3, about theta[1,1,1] being set to 0 and about an extra variance: blavaan is doing a parameter expansion thing in JAGS, where some extra latent variables are added to handle covariances between variables. So I think the thetas will not correspond exactly to what you would expect. Also, I believe that the thing being set to 1000 is a precision (vs a variance), which is approximately fixing the corresponding variance to 0 (to 1/1000). The issue is that JAGS would crash by fixing an observed variable variance to 0, so it gets fixed just above 0. And more detail about the parameter expansion is here:

https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v085i04

Your question 2, about estimates being off by a row: yes, it looks like the variances are off by a row for target="jags" but not for stan. I will have to fix something there.

Ed

messages.body_plain:
Thank you very much, Ed. I took your suggestion and standardized the data, then refit the model using blavaan (via targets = stan and JAGS) and the JAGS model file written by blavaan (via the jagsUI package). A few follow-up points:

1) With the exception of the issue with variances being off by a row, the blavaan estimates with targets = stan and jags are pretty consistent with the lavaan output, with good convergence. So standardization helped a lot in JAGs, even using the default prior options in blavaan.

2) When I fit the model using the JAGS file written by blavaan (using the same MCMC parameters and priors as blavaan), the parameter estimates are not consistent with those from blavaan or lavaan, and there are significant convergence issues.

3) I think I tracked down the issue in the JAGS file output from blavaan. The parameter being set to 1000 is psi[1,1,1], but I don't think that's a precision. It looks like the psi parameters are variances for the latent variables (e.g., eta[i, 1] ~ dnorm(mu_eta[i,1], 1/psi[3,3,g[i]]). The quantity 1/psi in the code is set as the precision, so psi must be the variance (precision = 1/variance). So I don't think it's correct to set the variance to 1000. The variance term should be constrained to something like 0.001. However, I don't think psi is the correct variance parameter to constrain in this case, as it's the error variance for an endogenous latent variable. Instead, I think the correct parameter to constrain is alpha[1,1,1], which corresponds to the error variance for the observed indicator "abu", which is the only indicator for the latent variable "abundance". I modified the JAGS code to make those changes, and the output was qualitatively similar to the blavaan output and lavaan output, and with very good convergence.

Below I've pasted a comparison of the estimates from the various model fits, as well is the original JAGS code produced by blavaan and the version that I modified. It's strange that blavaan reports seemingly correct parameter estimates with solid convergence when target = jags, whereas using the JAGS file output seems to produce very different estimates with poor convergence. Perhaps an issue with how the JAGS file output is being written. In any case, I'm encouraged that the modifications I made to the JAGS file seem to work, but please let me know if you see any issues with the changes I made.

Many thanks,
Brad

########JAGS FILE PRODUCED BY BLAVAAN#########
I flagged where I think corrections are needed.

model {
  for(i in 1:N) {
    abu[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i,1], 1/theta[1,1,g[i]])  #theta variance should be constrained
    mean_CC[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i,2], 1/theta[2,2,g[i]])
    mean_Food[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i,3], 1/theta[3,3,g[i]])
    mean_UI[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i,4], 1/theta[4,4,g[i]])
    dist.city[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i,5], 1/theta[5,5,g[i]])

    # lvs
    eta[i,1] ~ dnorm(mu_eta[i,1], 1/psi[3,3,g[i]])
    eta[i,2] <- mu_eta[i,2]   #should not be constrained
    eta[i,3] ~ dnorm(mu_eta[i,3], 1/psi[2,2,g[i]])
  }

  # mu definitions
  for(i in 1:N) {
    mu[i,1] <- nu[1,1,g[i]] + lambda[1,1,g[i]]*eta[i,2]
    mu[i,2] <- nu[2,1,g[i]] + lambda[2,2,g[i]]*eta[i,3]
    mu[i,3] <- nu[3,1,g[i]] + lambda[3,2,g[i]]*eta[i,3]
    mu[i,4] <- nu[4,1,g[i]] + lambda[4,3,g[i]]*eta[i,1]
    mu[i,5] <- nu[5,1,g[i]] + lambda[5,3,g[i]]*eta[i,1]

    mu_eta[i,1] <- alpha[3,1,g[i]]
    mu_eta[i,2] <- alpha[1,1,g[i]] + beta[1,2,g[i]]*eta[i,3] + beta[1,3,g[i]]*eta[i,1]
    mu_eta[i,3] <- alpha[2,1,g[i]] + beta[2,3,g[i]]*eta[i,1]
  }

  # Assignments from parameter vector & equality constraints
  lambda[1,1,1] <- 1
  lambda[2,2,1] <- 1
  lambda[3,2,1] <- parvec.dnorm[1]
  lambda[4,3,1] <- 1
  lambda[5,3,1] <- parvec.dnorm[2]
  beta[2,3,1] <- parvec.dnorm[3]
  beta[1,2,1] <- parvec.dnorm[4]
  beta[1,3,1] <- parvec.dnorm[5]
  theta[1,1,1] <- pow(parvec.dgamma[1],-1)  #indicator variance - should be constrained to 0.001
  theta[2,2,1] <- pow(parvec.dgamma[2],-1)
  theta[3,3,1] <- pow(parvec.dgamma[3],-1)
  theta[4,4,1] <- pow(parvec.dgamma[4],-1)
  theta[5,5,1] <- pow(parvec.dgamma[5],-1)
  psi[1,1,1] <- 1000  #latent variance - I don't think this should be constrained.
  psi[2,2,1] <- pow(parvec.dgamma[6],-1)
  psi[3,3,1] <- pow(parvec.dgamma[7],-1)
  nu[1,1,1] <- parvec.dnorm[6]
  nu[2,1,1] <- parvec.dnorm[7]
  nu[3,1,1] <- parvec.dnorm[8]
  nu[4,1,1] <- parvec.dnorm[9]
  nu[5,1,1] <- parvec.dnorm[10]
  alpha[1,1,1] <- 0
  alpha[2,1,1] <- 0
  alpha[3,1,1] <- 0
  # Priors
  parvec.dnorm[1] ~ dnorm(0,1e-2)
  parvec.dnorm[2] ~ dnorm(0,1e-2)
  parvec.dnorm[3] ~ dnorm(0,1e-2)
  parvec.dnorm[4] ~ dnorm(0,1e-2)
  parvec.dnorm[5] ~ dnorm(0,1e-2)
  parvec.dgamma[1] ~ dgamma(1,.5)
  parvec.dgamma[2] ~ dgamma(1,.5)
  parvec.dgamma[3] ~ dgamma(1,.5)
  parvec.dgamma[4] ~ dgamma(1,.5)
  parvec.dgamma[5] ~ dgamma(1,.5)
  parvec.dgamma[6] ~ dgamma(1,.5)
  parvec.dgamma[7] ~ dgamma(1,.5)
  parvec.dnorm[6] ~ dnorm(0,1e-3)
  parvec.dnorm[7] ~ dnorm(0,1e-3)
  parvec.dnorm[8] ~ dnorm(0,1e-3)
  parvec.dnorm[9] ~ dnorm(0,1e-3)
  parvec.dnorm[10] ~ dnorm(0,1e-3)
}
